children: Marygold reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $25.3 million, an 8% increase from $23.4 million in fiscal 2025, and narrowed its net loss to $4.4 million, or $0.10 per share. For the fourth quarter ended June 30, 2026, revenue rose 26% year-over-year to $6.9 million while the quarter’s net loss was $3.7 million, driven largely by non-cash impairments. The company ended the year with $2.9 million in cash and stockholders’ equity of $19.2 million.
Revenue for fiscal 2026: $25.3 million, up from $23.4 million in fiscal 2025.
Gross profit for fiscal 2026: $23.449 million (as reported).
Operating loss (total operating expenses exceeded gross profit): loss from continuing operations $(6.012) million.
Net loss for fiscal 2026: $(4.371) million (reported net loss); net loss per share: $(0.10) basic and diluted.
Balance sheet at June 30, 2026: total assets $23.979 million; cash and cash equivalents $2.880 million; stockholders’ equity $19.226 million.
USCF Investments delivered strong growth with revenue up 23% and average assets under management rising 41% to $4.1 billion for the year, driven by higher energy-related commodity prices.
Original Sprout returned to profitability and achieved 13% revenue growth following a transformation of its sales strategy to match changing customer shopping preferences.

Company executed strategic portfolio moves: New Zealand subsidiaries were designated as discontinued operations and put up for sale, the Canadian security business was sold, and fintech operations in the U.S. and U.K. were paused.

Fiscal 2026 included significant non-cash impairments: write-off of intangible assets related to U.K. financial services and impairment of an illiquid investment, which materially impacted quarterly and annual operating results.
